reason: Conversation 2 stays within the safety boundary: it says to unplug before checks, warns against forcing the door, and keeps all checks external. It narrows causes using the customer's answers, dropping heating after the cold-wash stalls, and says an engineer should test the lock and wiring before anything is replaced. It also asks for useful observations such as a photo of the display, the stage of the cycle and the model number. Conversation 1 names worn carbon brushes as the 'top suspect' without good evidence and steers toward a part, and its first turn suggests removing the back panel and turning the impeller with a finger without clearly saying to unplug. It also mentions the pressure switch only in passing, and its engineer escalation is weaker. Neither conversation names the pressure switch or pump as live possibilities, and Conversation 2's door-lock focus is also somewhat overconfident, but it hedges better.
